data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
learningPoints: Builds accurate use of first, second, and zero conditionals.
Develops reasoning skills for real and hypothetical situations.
Strengthens problem-solving language for interviews and tests.
Improves logical thinking in speaking and writing tasks.
Prepares you for opinion and consequence-based exam questions.
ESOL B2 and aligns with IELTS 6.0–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72–94 score ranges.

sections.explain: Second conditional: 'if' + past simple, then 'would' + base verb. Don't use present 'win' or future 'will'.

words.word: If I win the lottery, I would buy a house.
If I won the lottery, I would buy a house.
If I won the lottery, I will buy a house.

sections.summary: Second conditional for unreal present situations.
sections.explain: Use past simple in the if-clause and 'would' in the result. 'would' is not used in the if-clause.

words.word: If he would speak French, he would move to Paris.
If he spoke French, he would move to Paris.
If he spoke French, he will move to Paris.

sections.explain: Second conditional uses past simple + would + base verb.

words.word: If I had more time, I would travel more.
If I have more time, I would travel more.
If I would have more time, I travel more.

sections.explain: 'if' + past simple, then 'would' + base verb: 'would swim'. Present 'live' and 'would swimming' are wrong.

words.word: If we live by the sea, we would swim every day.
If we lived by the sea, we would swimming every day.
If we lived by the sea, we would swim every day.

sections.explain: Use past simple after 'if' even for present unreal situations.

words.word: If she knew the answer, she would tell us.
If she knows the answer, she would tell us.
If she would know the answer, she tells us.

sections.explain: Past simple in the if-clause, 'would' + base verb in the result. 'would know' and 'would called' are incorrect.

words.word: If I would know her number, I would call her.
If I knew her number, I would called her.
If I knew her number, I would call her.
If I were you, I would accept the offer.
If I was you, I will accept the offer.
If I am you, I would accept the offer.

sections.explain: 'if' + past simple, then 'would' + base verb: 'would accept'. Present 'offer' and 'would accepted' are wrong.

words.word: If they offer me the job, I would accept it.
If they offered me the job, I would accept it.
If they offered me the job, I would accepted it.

sections.summary: Second conditional with 'were' for all subjects.
sections.explain: In the second conditional 'were' is used for all subjects: 'If she were taller'. The result uses 'would', not 'will'.

words.word: If she were taller, she would play basketball.
If she was taller, she would play basketball.
If she were taller, she will play basketball.

sections.summary: Contrast between first and second conditional.
sections.explain: Use first conditional for real future; second conditional for unreal situations.

words.word: If she studies hard, she will pass; if she studied harder, she would get a scholarship.
If she studies hard, she would pass; if she studied harder, she will get a scholarship.
If she will study hard, she will pass; if she studied harder, she would get a scholarship.
